The Beman Project: Testing C++ Library Proposals Before Standardization - Dietmar Kühl - ACCU 2025 Short Talks
---

How do C++ library proposals mature before becoming part of the C++ standard library? In this ACCU 2025 lightning talk, Dietmar Kühl introduces the Beman Project — a community-driven initiative to test and validate C++ standard library proposals before they’re accepted into the standard.

The Beman Project acts as a proving ground for experimental libraries intended for the C++ standardization process. Inspired by the spirit of Boost, but designed for today’s evolving language and library ecosystem, Beman provides structured implementations of proposals such as `optional＜T&＞`, range-based extensions, execution libraries, and views and iterators.

Dietmar Kühl outlines how the Beman Project helps ensure proposals are viable, usable, and buildable — with consistent layout and integration patterns — before they reach the C+
